newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shopping mall begins new policy for children.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shopping mall begins new policy for children.

text.p: A shopping mall that claims to be the nation's largest instituted a policy Friday requiring children under age 16 to be accompanied by an adult on weekend nights.
But a group calling itself the Twin Cities chapter of Refuse and Resist said the Mall of America's policy was racist because many young unescorted visitors are black or Asian.
The group vowed to protest and provide adult escorts at the Bloomington, Minn., mall, a huge suburban indoor shopping centre where carnival rides attract millions of children each year.
Under the policy, unaccompanied youths will be asked to leave the mall Friday and Saturday evenings from 6 p.m. until the 9:30 p.m. closing. Those that resist could be arrested.
Security guards have been trained in "verbal judo" to equip them to deal with recalcitrant youngsters, mall officials said.
The policy resulted from increased reports of fights and threatening behaviour by young visitors, including an incident in June when chairs were thrown.
The mall has set up an area where adult volunteers will provide soft drinks and cookies, plus telephones for kids to call for rides. If they cannot find a ride, the mall will provide bus passes.
The mall also paid for an advertising campaign featuring an incredulous youth asking, "Bring my parents?"
Younger critics of the policy said older teenagers were responsible for incidents at the mall and argued the plan was unneccessary.
